summary: Full traffic system on world.roads lanes. A baked lane graph (per-edge, per-lane polylines sampled from world.roads.laneCenter, zero-allocation lookup) drives A* routing over the road graph, IDM car-following, turn-based lane assignment with smooth lane-change blending, traffic-signal phases at avenue/highway crossings (api.lightState(nodeId)), first-come junction reservation plus a keep-clear rule at unsignalised 3+ arm nodes, right-hand traffic and spill-back queueing. 8 procedural vehicle classes (sedan, hatchback, suv, taxi, pickup, van, truck, bus) are lofted from a monotone-cubic longitudinal profile into superellipse cross sections, so bodies have real windshield/roof curvature, a glass greenhouse with pillars and a beltline, dark wheel arches, headlight/taillight lenses and roof details (taxi sign, bus HVAC + destination blind, truck deflector). Each class is ONE InstancedMesh: material id per vertex picks paint/glass/tyre/rim/lens/trim, per-instance attributes carry the paint colour, the wheel spin angle (wheels rotate in the vertex shader) and the head/brake light intensities. Vehicles pitch with the road grade. At night an additive rig adds head/tail/brake glows plus ground light cones that hold a minimum apparent size so they still read from the aerial camera. Pedestrians walk the sidewalk polylines with a shader-driven walk cycle (legs/arms swing about hip/shoulder pivots, body bob) and pick the nearest sidewalk side at each node. Highway/avenue dead ends become outside connections that spawn and despawn external commuters and trucks. Counts scale with world.economy.population and the simulation activity(hour) curve (with an internal fallback). api: spawnVehicle/despawn/flowGrid (256^2 congestion)/lightState/signals/outsideConnections/kinds/stats/setTargets/preroll/setShadowCasting/serialize/deserialize; world.traffic.vehicles, .pedestrians and .stats are published live. Showcase stages the roads showcase network and pre-rolls 45 s of simulation so screenshots catch queues already formed; presets junction and highway_night added. IMPORTANT: real CSM shadow casting is currently OFF for vehicles and pedestrians because the engine's cascade shadows drop every occluder under ~3 m (measured, see docs/core-requests/traffic.md); soft contact-shadow decals ground them instead and api.setShadowCasting(true) restores real casting once the core bias is fixed.
remainingWeaknesses: No real cast shadows. The engine's CSM drops occluders under ~3 m (measured by lifting the vehicle group 0/1/2/4/8 m: shadows only appear from 4 m up), so vehicles never darken the road. Contact-shadow decals ground them from above but are almost invisible from the low street/skyline cameras, which is the single biggest realism gap vs CS2. Core request filed.

Vehicle bodies are smooth but under-detailed: no door shut lines, mirrors, separate bumpers/grille, number plates or wheel-arch lips; the glass is a flat dark band with no interior or seat silhouettes. At closeup they read like stylised 1950s cars rather than modern CS2 traffic.
No parked cars along kerbs, no bicycles, motorbikes, emergency or service vehicles; CS2 streets are visually much busier at the roadside than mine are.
Pedestrians do not use crosswalks or wait at signals; at a junction they jump from the end of one sidewalk to the start of the next, which pops if you watch one closely at street level.

Signalised junctions have no visible traffic-light heads — api.lightState(nodeId) is published for props to consume, but nothing in the traffic showcase draws them, so from a still frame a queue at a red light looks unexplained.
Headlight glows are faint from the aerial camera at 22:00; the minimum-apparent-size clamp (2.4x) is tuned for the street/closeup cameras and could go to ~4x for far views.

Traffic density at noon still reads a little sparse in the residential grid compared with CS2 (about 135 vehicles over ~4 km of network); the mix is also car-heavy with no visible car-following variety like tailgating or overtaking on the highway.
No wet-road response: world.weather.rain/wetness is ignored, so no spray, no reflected head/tail lights on wet asphalt.
Lane changes only happen at edge entry (blended over up to 30 m); vehicles never overtake mid-block, so a slow truck holds up a whole lane on the highway.
fps is 10-11.6 under SwiftShader software GL only; real-GPU fps is unmeasured (fpsGpu null).
